newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Public Bank sees 20 pct rise in profit.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank sees 20 pct rise in profit.

text.p: Public Bank Bhd's chief executive officer said he expects the company to post a 20 percent rise in net profit for 1997 compared with a year ago.
"As you can see, we make moderate increases every year," said Teh Hong Tiow, who is also the bank's president following Public Bank's annual general meeting.
"A reasonable assumption would be that our (net) profit will be 20 percent higher over 1996," he said.
Public Bank's year ends in December. For calendar 1996, Malaysia's third largest bank reported 408.02 million ringgit in net profit.
Answering questions about the bank's exposure to property and share lending, its chairman Thong Yaw Hong said the company was within limits set by central bank Bank Negara at the end of March.
"We are well within the limit prescribed by Bank Negara," Thong said. "In case of property, it is well below 15 percent, and in case of shares, well below 10 percent," he told reporters.
The central bank imposed the limits, effective April 1, to quell asset speculation.
